notes: Tier 1 (direct HTTP via curl/WebFetch) hard-blocked: shopterrain.com is protected by DataDome bot-protection which returns HTTP 403 with a captcha-delivery interstitial for every request, including robots.txt itself. Escalated to Claude-in-Chrome (tier 3, no separate Playwright/CDP tool available in this environment). Loaded robots.txt through the browser (it rendered fine there): generic 'User-agent: * / Allow: /' with only /orchestration/, /api/, /cgi-bin/, /blog/wp-content/, /homepage disallowed and no Claude-specific rule - not a policy opt-out, so browser access proceeded. Discovery method: fetched sitemapindex.xml -> categories_sitemap.xml (full list of ~280 category/facet URLs reviewed) to enumerate every candidate seasonal slug, then visited each candidate PLP directly via navigate+get_page_text, reading the site's own displayed 'N products' total, breadcrumb and on-page copy. Terrain runs a very large seasonal program (Sept 2026 = deep into Fall/Halloween season, Christmas 'sneak peek' already live): Halloween and the general Christmas/'Holiday' collection each have one broad hub PLP plus several curated, heavily product-overlapping trend/theme sub-shops (verified overlap directly: e.g. 'Witches Brew Cauldron Candle' and 'Mouse Witch Illuminated Felt Critter' appear in both /halloween-shop and /spellcasters-shop; '5" Colorful Glass Bauble Ornaments, Set of 6' appears in /shop-all-holiday, /holiday-tree-ornaments, /stocking-fillers, /cheerfull-holiday-decor and /merrimint-holiday-decor). Per the parent/subset rule, the broad hub row for each (Halloween Shop 348; Shop All Holiday/'Holiday Sneak Peek' 814) is kept as an is_group:true row (real displayed qty retained, per the hoeffner.de precedent, not nulled) with each named theme/product-type sub-shop as its own is_group:false child row using its own displayed qty - none of the qty values were summed by me. Mother's Day and Father's Day were evaluated under the same genuine-PLP test as any other holiday per explicit instruction (both are real, well-developed, site-named PLPs with their own facet filters and pagination: 342 and 230 products respectively) and kept. Fall was evaluated per the explicit Fall/Autumn guidance: /fall-shop ('The Fall Decor Shop', 461 products) sits on identical structural footing to /halloween-shop - same '-shop' URL pattern, same dedicated facet/filter/pagination PLP chrome, same homepage promotional treatment ('visit the fall shop' next to 'visit the Halloween shop') - so it was kept as a genuine first-class Fall occasion row. By contrast /summer-celebrations ('Summer Décor + Entertaining Essentials', 109 products) was evaluated and EXCLUDED: it names no specific festival/celebration (no July 4th, solstice, etc.), uses a different URL pattern than the '-shop' occasion pages, and reads as a generic outdoor-entertaining seasonal merchandising page functionally overlapping the existing year-round 'Outdoor Living' nav category rather than a distinct holiday - it fails criterion 2 (site does not itself name a specific holiday/festival for this node). /easter (title 'Easter Decor + Gifts', full descriptive copy, no breadcrumb count) currently shows 'Sorry, no products were found for this category' - kept as a genuine qty:0 row (page infrastructure, title and marketing copy all confirm the node genuinely exists in the taxonomy; it is simply off-season in early September) per the same logic used for other companies' off-season zero-count Christmas nodes. Checked and EXCLUDED as non-genuine: /halloween-decorating (editorial/lookbook hub page with no product grid or count, links out to the real /halloween-shop PLP - a landing page, not itself a PLP); /apothecary-shop ('Apothecary Trend Shop', 73 products, entirely Halloween-themed content by inspection but the page's own title/breadcrumb never names Halloween or any holiday - a generic aesthetic trend shop, fails criterion 2); /kaleidoscope-shop and /sweet-shop (both dead sitemap entries, resolve to the site's 404 'Hmm...' page); /holiday-lighting (redirects to the same content as /holiday-wreaths - not a distinct page, not double counted); /holiday-gifts (redirects to /terrain-holiday-house, which is separately listed below under its real title/URL). Also present in the sitemap but not seasonal/holiday and excluded as ordinary year-round categories: /wedding-decor-favors-gifts, /new-house-home, /martha-stewart-favorites, /mushroom-gifts, /bee-shop, /birding-shop, /birding, /arcadia-shop, /fawn-and-fable-shop, /the-farmers-market, and the many generic /gifts-* (spa-beauty, candles, bouquets-flowers, accessories, etc.) and /sale-* pages - none of these name a specific holiday. No Diwali, Independence Day/July 4th, Cinco de Mayo, Lunar New Year, or similar festival slugs exist anywhere in the sitemap (consistent with a US garden/home brand). Standard storewide 'Labor Day' 30%-off promo banner seen on the homepage was excluded as a sale campaign, not a seasonal category.
